headline: UNEP Maps 2030 and 2040 Cuts for 1.5°C Return
deck: A UN pathway gives a roughly 50% chance of returning warming to 1.5°C or lower by 2100 after a mid-century peak.
body: The UN Environment Programme said its lowest-possible 1.5°C overshoot scenario would limit peak warming around mid-century to 1.7–1.8°C, then return global temperature rise to or below 1.5°C by 2100 with about a 50% chance. [E1]
The pathway requires emissions cuts of 18% by 2030 and 45% by 2035, alongside increasing carbon-dioxide removal throughout the century, UNEP said. [E2]

Inger Andersen, UNEP’s executive director, said cutting global carbon emissions by 18% by 2030 and 69% by 2040 was the only route back to a future that remained “largely manageable without major impacts.” [E3]

evidence_box.fragment: The Emissions Gap Report 2026: The Point of Return looks at a ‘lowest possible’ 1.5°C overshoot scenario, in which peak warming by around the middle of the century is limited to 1.7-1.8°C and global temperature rise is returned to or below 1.5°C by 2100, with about a 50 per cent chance.
